title: The Niche for Lights
author: Al-Ghazali (Gairdner trans)
description: Al-Ghazzali's Mishkat al-Anwar (The Niche for Lights), translated with an introduction by W. H. T. Gairdner (Royal Asiatic Society, Asiatic Society Monographs, 1924). In this short and profound late work, al-Ghazali comments on the 'Light Verse' of the Qur'an (24:35), 'God is the Light of the heavens and the earth; the similitude of His light is as a niche wherein is a lamp...', and on the hadith of the seventy thousand veils of light and darkness. He argues that God alone is light in the true sense, that all other lights are borrowed from Him, and interprets the niche, glass, lamp, tree and oil as the levels of human perception: sense, imagination, reason, reflection and prophetic spirit. He classifies seekers according to the veils that separate them from God. Gairdner's introduction discusses the work's Neoplatonic character and its influence on later illuminationist and Sufi metaphysics.
